title: AT&T shareholders vote against approving executive compensation
summary: AT&T shareholders have voted against approving executive compensation during the company's annual meeting, with only 49% of votes cast in favor. This advisory vote comes as executive pay packages have grown, and highlights shareholder concerns, particularly regarding the more than $52 million compensation for WarnerMedia CEO Jason Kilar, which was double that of AT&T CEO John Stankey. AT&T's board acknowledged the vote and stated they would consider it to ensure their compensation approach aligns with company principles.

title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway rebounds from pandemic with $11.7 billion profit
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway announced a net profit of $11.7 billion in the first quarter of 2021, recovering from a significant loss in early 2020 due to the pandemic. The conglomerate, which owns diverse businesses, saw strong revenue growth as the economy reopened. Despite a massive cash pile of $145.4 billion, Berkshire Hathaway continued significant stock buybacks rather than pursuing large acquisitions, even as its stock performance has lagged the broader market in recent years.

title: Bracing for a record pool chlorine shortage in summer 2021
summary: Pool owners are facing a record chlorine shortage in summer 2021 due to a pandemic-driven increase in demand and a fire at a major chemical plant. This has led to steep price increases for chlorine tablets, with some retailers advising customers to stock up now or consider alternative sanitization methods like saltwater systems or liquid chlorine. The shortage is impacting corporate earnings and is expected to continue through the peak pool season.

title: 2021 Tech Titans
summary: This article highlights the 2021 Tech Titans in Washington D.C.'s digital economy, recognizing over 170 influential leaders, innovators, and officials who demonstrated resilience and growth despite the pandemic. It showcases entrepreneurs who launched new companies, secured significant funding, and adapted their businesses, along with key figures in finance, cybersecurity, government, and policy. The piece also acknowledges leaders in the satellite, telecommunications, and defense industries who are shaping the region's tech landscape.

title: Kroger delivery takes to the skies with drone pilot
summary: Kroger is launching a drone delivery pilot program this spring, starting with test flights near a Kroger Marketplace in Centerville, Ohio, and expanding to a Ralphs location in California in the summer. The program will utilize autonomous drones from Drone Express to deliver groceries weighing up to 5 pounds within 15 minutes, directly to consumers' locations within flight range. This initiative follows similar efforts by Amazon and Walmart, as Kroger aims to enhance its online fulfillment ecosystem and compete in the rapidly evolving grocery delivery market.

title: Google to power Virginia data centers with 24/7 clean energy from AES
summary: AES has signed a 10-year agreement to exclusively supply 24/7 clean energy to three Google data centers in Virginia, utilizing a 500-MW portfolio of resources. This partnership aims to decarbonize Google's operations in the state and sets a precedent for other companies seeking to eliminate carbon from their energy supply. The AES portfolio will require approximately $600 million for its clean energy projects.

title: Boeing is giving Virginia Tech $50 million to help launch new campus
summary: Boeing has pledged a $50 million multiyear donation to Virginia Tech, marking the largest corporate gift in the university's history. This funding is intended to support financial aid and other initiatives for Virginia Tech's new graduate technology campus in Northern Virginia, with a focus on building and diversifying the student body. The investment highlights growing corporate interest in educational projects near major business hubs, such as Amazon's new headquarters.

title: AVODs double down on original programming, content studios at NewFronts
summary: Several ad-supported video on demand (AVOD) services, including Tubi, IMDb TV, Crackle Plus, and fuboTV, announced significant investment in original programming and content studios at the IAB NewFronts. This move comes as AVODs experience increased viewership and advertiser interest, driven by changing consumer behavior during the pandemic and a desire for alternatives to subscription-based services. Companies are leveraging these new offerings and enhanced targeting capabilities to attract both viewers and advertisers.

title: JD Logistics approved for IPO; spinoff could raise $4B
summary: JD Logistics, the logistics arm of Chinese e-commerce giant JD.com, has received approval for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, potentially raising up to $4 billion. This follows JD Health International's successful IPO. Despite significant investments in automation and technology leading to a net loss in 2020, the company aims for profitability through customer expansion, leveraging its extensive warehouse network and advanced logistics capabilities to support JD.com's growth in China's fragmented retail market.

title: Televisa y TV Azteca se recuperan en publicidad, pero toca impulsar el contenido
summary: Televisa and TV Azteca are seeing a recovery in advertising revenue after a challenging 2020, with Televisa's ad income up 28.1% and TV Azteca's up 8% in Q1 2021. However, despite increased viewership during the COVID-19 pandemic, both companies face the challenge of migrating advertising investment to digital platforms and the need to innovate content to retain audiences and compete with streaming services. Experts emphasize that investing in new, high-quality content is crucial for the future of open television.

title: Jessica Alba’s Honest Co. IPO soars on $1.4 billion valuation
summary: Jessica Alba's The Honest Company Inc. made its public debut, with its IPO raising over $412 million and valuing the company at $1.4 billion. The stock, trading under the ticker HNST, saw a significant pop of over 40% on its first day. The wellness brand, founded in 2011, offers clean beauty, baby products, and household items, and has expanded its retail presence.

title: Drivers don't work for Amazon but company has lots of rules for them
summary: Amazon exerts significant control over its Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) and their drivers, despite not directly employing them, dictating everything from personal grooming to social media posts. This "fissured" labor model helps Amazon avoid costs and liabilities, but legal experts warn it could lead to "joint employer" or "vicarious liability" claims, especially under closer scrutiny in the Biden administration. The company faces ongoing lawsuits regarding wage theft and accountability for accidents, highlighting the controversial nature of its delivery operations.

title: Amazon Work Rules Govern Tweets, Body Odor of Contract Drivers
summary: Amazon dictates extensive rules for its contract delivery drivers, covering aspects from personal grooming and social media posts to mandatory training and drug testing. These detailed policies, despite drivers being employed by independent partners, raise questions about potential legal and regulatory challenges given the level of control Amazon exerts over these workers. The company's efforts to standardize its vast delivery network could lead to scrutiny over employment classifications.

title: Strategy Analytics: Amazon's Ring Claimed Top Spot in Global Home Security Camera Market in 2020
summary: In 2020, Amazon's Ring successfully doubled its market share and became the leading smart home security camera brand globally, surpassing Arlo and Wyze, according to Strategy Analytics. This growth was attributed to an aggressive expansion of its camera portfolio, particularly spotlight-equipped outdoor and indoor cameras, capitalizing on the brand's strong reputation from its video doorbells. The report also highlights the other top five brands as Arlo, Wyze, Google’s Nest, and Alarm.com, noting a total of 42.5 million cameras shipped to consumers in 2020 by all brands combined.

title: The Honest Company Founder Jessica Alba Rings The Bell
summary: Lightspeed Venture Partners celebrates The Honest Company's IPO, reflecting on its journey from a mission-driven startup founded by Jessica Alba in 2011 to a public company. The article highlights the company's initial rapid growth, subsequent challenges, and its return to profitability under CEO Nick Vlahos's leadership. Lightspeed expresses pride in supporting Honest Company's commitment to clean and conscious innovation.

title: Five Guys, Several New Businesses Coming To North Haven: Freda
summary: North Haven First Selectman Michael Freda announced that several new businesses, including a Five Guys restaurant, a Starbucks with a drive-thru, and an O’Reilly’s Auto Parts Store, are coming to the town. Additionally, a new Mexican restaurant called Torito, a Hampton Inn, Panera Bread, and Jersey Mike’s Subs are planned for Universal Drive and other locations. These developments are part of an effort to grow the town's grand list and enhance consumer services.

title: Jessica Alba's Honest Co. surges in Nasdaq debut
summary: Jessica Alba's eco-friendly personal care brand, Honest Co. (HNST), saw its shares surge 44% in its Nasdaq debut, closing at $23 per share and giving the company a market value of about $2.1 billion. CEO Nick Vlahos viewed the successful IPO as validation of the company's mission-driven strategy focused on clean, sustainable, and socially responsible products. Despite its growth in sales to over $300 million in 2020 and narrowing net losses, the company has not yet turned a profit and has previously faced controversial lawsuits regarding its product labeling.

title: Iron Mountain joins The Climate Pledge
summary: Iron Mountain has joined The Climate Pledge, committing to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040, a decade ahead of the Paris Agreement's goal. As an information and asset management business, Iron Mountain has already significantly reduced its greenhouse gas emissions and aims for 100% clean power generation for its data centers. This move signifies its dedication to environmental impact reduction and aligns with over 100 other companies in the pledge.

title: Wealth Advisors Value Human Interaction and Technology
summary: Wealth advisors are navigating evolving client expectations, particularly from younger generations who prioritize digital experiences. A FactSet survey highlights that while technology adoption is crucial for efficiency and managing relationships, human interaction remains vital for discussing client goals and market conditions. Advisors are seeking consolidated, intuitive, and integrated platforms to enhance their effectiveness and proactively engage with clients.

title: Transformers Kingdom Airazor Concept Art by Ken Christiansen
summary: Ken Christiansen has shared new concept art for the Transformers Kingdom series, specifically featuring Airazor. The artwork includes notes from Christiansen and was commissioned in partnership with Hasbro, Inc. The original art drawings are now available on Hasbro Pulse.

title: Amazon Sidewalk is About to Strengthen the Finding Power of Your Tiles
summary: This short article announces that Amazon Sidewalk will enhance the tracking capabilities of Tile devices. It suggests that users will benefit from a stronger finding network for their Tiles.

title: NRG Energy names Houston sole HQ, hires CFO from 'Amazon of South Korea'
summary: NRG Energy has officially designated Houston as its sole headquarters, a shift from its previous dual-headquarters structure shared with Princeton, New Jersey, since 2012. Concurrently, the company has announced the hiring of a new Chief Financial Officer from Coupang, an e-commerce company dubbed the "Amazon of South Korea." This move follows NRG's acquisition of Houston-based GenOn and marks a significant step in centralizing its operations in Texas.

title: Office Depot parent plans to break up its retail and B2B businesses
summary: Office Depot's parent company plans to separate its retail (ODP) and business-to-business (NewCo) units into two independent, publicly traded companies. This move aims to maximize the strategic focus and financial flexibility of each entity, as their trajectories have diverged over the years, further highlighted by the pandemic's impact on their respective sales. The separation is expected to be completed in the first half of 2022, following similar actions by Staples' parent company.

title: 3 Reasons Pinduoduo Stock Fell by More Than 30% in 2021
summary: Pinduoduo's stock fell by over 30% in 2021 due to three main factors: the surprising departure of its founder and chairman Zheng Huang, increased regulatory scrutiny on Chinese tech companies, and a broader market shift away from high-growth tech stocks towards "reopening" plays. Despite these short-term challenges, the company's long-term prospects remain strong, with plans to expand customer spending on its platform and grow its agriculture-related gross merchandise value significantly by 2025. New CEO Lei Chen, part of the original team, is expected to continue driving the company's growth.

title: Help With Vaccination Push Comes From Unexpected Businesses (Published 2021)
summary: Major companies like Microsoft, Starbucks, and Amazon are assisting the government's COVID-19 vaccination efforts by offering logistical support, physical locations, and operational expertise. These companies, despite not being directly in healthcare, are leveraging their vast resources, national footprints, and distribution networks to help with the rollout. This private sector involvement aims to boost the vaccination drive and could enhance the companies' public image and bottom line.

title: Sanctions-as-a-Service: US Regulators Escalate Sanctions Enforcement Priorities Into the Cloud with SAP Settlement
authors: ['John P. Barker', 'John B. Bellinger', 'III', 'Soo-Mi Rhee', 'Baruch Weiss', 'Nicholas L. Townsend', 'Tal R. Machnes', 'Alyssa T. Gerstner', 'Trevor G. Schmitt']
summary: US regulators announced a global resolution with SAP SE following its voluntary disclosure of providing software and cloud-based services to users in Iran, violating export and sanctions regulations. This settlement, involving the Departments of Justice, Commerce, and Treasury, highlights the US government's increased focus on sanctions compliance in the tech sector, particularly regarding cloud-based services and the need for robust screening and access controls. SAP agreed to pay over $8 million in penalties and invested over $27 million in enhancing its compliance programs.

title: Sectors Disrupted: Breaking E-commerce Out of the Box
summary: The article discusses investment opportunities in e-commerce, presenting it as an alternative to traditional consumer discretionary or technology investments. It highlights ProShares ETFs like EMTY, CLIX, and ONLN, which allow investors to capitalize on the growth of online retail and the decline of brick-and-mortar stores. A webcast is announced where experts will further discuss these themes and strategies.

title: Metro East distribution center to undergo $7M expansion
summary: TriStar Properties is investing $7 million to expand a distribution center in Edwardsville, Illinois, leased by Phillips 66. The project will add 60,000 square feet to the existing 102,500-square-foot facility within the Gateway Commerce Center. This expansion is expected to increase the building's value to approximately $18 million once completed in October.

title: Amazon borrows $18.5 billion it doesn’t need in new debt sale
summary: Amazon.com Inc. issued $18.5 billion in new debt, its largest bond sale ever, despite holding $73 billion in cash and cash equivalents. The company is taking advantage of historically low borrowing costs to refinance debt, buy back stock, and fund general corporate purposes, including potential acquisitions and green projects. This move highlights a trend among U.S. investment-grade firms to secure cheap financing for growth and strategic initiatives as the economy rebounds.

title: Dealmaker: JBG Smith, J.P. Morgan Global Alternatives Form Joint Venture for Potomac Yard Redevelopment
summary: JBG Smith and J.P. Morgan Global Alternatives have formed a joint venture to redevelop nearly two million square feet of mixed-use space in Potomac Yard, Alexandria, VA, near Amazon's future HQ2 and Virginia Tech's Innovation Campus. JBG Smith will contribute land and serve as developer, property manager, and leasing agent, expanding its ownership in National Landing. The project includes two multifamily buildings set to begin construction within 12 months, with the entire site accessible via the new Potomac Yard Metro station.

title: MySize debuts virtual fit avatar tool
summary: MySize, an e-commerce measurement tech startup, has launched a new avatar feature that allows online shoppers to virtually try on clothes. This tool aims to reduce returns, which have become more common and costly with the surge in e-commerce, by helping customers visualize how garments will fit without sharing personal photos. The company hopes this "gamification" will enhance the interactive shopping experience and build customer loyalty.

title: GaN IC maker Navitas to go public
summary: Navitas Semiconductor, a GaN power IC company, is set to go public by merging with Live Oak Acquisition Corp II, a special purpose acquisition company. The transaction values the combined entity at $1.4 billion, enabling Navitas to expand its reach from mobile and consumer markets into more power-intensive applications. Navitas has already shipped integrated circuits to major companies such as Dell, LG, and Amazon.

title: AWS, HPE, Other IT Vendors Back $50B Call For U.S. Chip Production
summary: A coalition including major IT vendors like AWS, HPE, Apple, and Microsoft is advocating for $50 billion in U.S. government funding for domestic semiconductor manufacturing and research. This initiative, part of the CHIPS for America Act, aims to address the decline in U.S. chip production share and bolster supply chain resiliency. While supporting the funding, the group advised against government intervention in the current chip shortage and urged careful allocation of funds to benefit the entire industry rather than individual companies.

title: Wheels Up Taps Former Amazon and Airbnb Executive Vinayak Hegde as Chief Marketplace Officer
summary: Wheels Up, a leading private aviation brand, has appointed Vinayak Hegde, formerly of Amazon and Airbnb, as its Chief Marketplace Officer. In this role, Hegde will be responsible for the strategy and execution of Wheels Up's marketplace initiatives, including revenue, product, technology, business strategy, sales, and member experience. His expertise in scaling consumer internet offerings is expected to help Wheels Up expand its private aviation platform and increase accessibility.

title: Wealthfront Adds Marketing Powerhouse Jaleh Bisharat to Board of Directors
summary: Wealthfront announced that marketing executive and entrepreneur Jaleh Bisharat has joined its Board of Directors. Bisharat brings over 30 years of experience with consumer brands like Amazon, Eventbrite, OpenTable, and Upwork, and is also the co-founder and CEO of NakedPoppy. Her expertise will be instrumental in expanding Wealthfront's reach and supporting its technology-driven approach to financial services.

title: Streaming Giants Are Spending Billions Overseas. Here Comes the Pushback.
summary: U.S.-based streaming services like Netflix, Amazon, Disney+, and HBO Max are investing billions in overseas markets to produce local-language content, leading to a boom for local talent and increased competition. However, this global expansion is also generating pushback from established international broadcasters, local lawmakers, and producers who are raising concerns about equal pay and content ownership. This development occurs as Disney+ has boosted its parent company's stock, highlighting the significant impact of streaming in the entertainment industry.

title: Netgear WN3000RP vs Linksys RE6500: which Wi-Fi extender is better?
summary: This article compares two Wi-Fi extenders, the Netgear WN3000RP and the Linksys RE6500, to help consumers choose the best option for their needs and budget. It highlights their different features, target markets, and benefits, noting that the Netgear is a more affordable entry-level option, while the Linksys is a high-end device with superior range and speed. The piece concludes by recommending the Netgear for basic signal extension and the Linksys for more demanding users seeking advanced capabilities.

title: To All The Things Lana Condor Has Loved Before, Including Her Favorite Lip Balm
summary: Actress and producer Lana Condor discusses her collaboration with Vera Bradley for their new Recycled Cotton collection, including a limited-edition backpack she designed. She shares insights into her favorite everyday items, from her go-to lip balm and best jeans to unexpected product discoveries and sentimental gifts. The article highlights her personal style and recommendations.

title: Safaricom in Talks With U.S. Giant Amazon on Mobile Payments
summary: Safaricom Plc, Kenya's largest company, is in discussions with Amazon.com Inc. to integrate its M-Pesa mobile-money service onto Amazon's e-commerce platform. This move is part of Safaricom's strategy to expand its global reach and recover from its first profit decline in a decade, viewing fintech as a crucial driver for sales. The talks aim to enable M-Pesa payments for online retail purchases.

title: JPMorgan Is America’s Largest Company In 2021, But Amazon Is Rising In The Ranks
summary: Despite a pandemic, America's largest companies grew significantly in 2021, with JPMorgan Chase maintaining its position as the largest for the third consecutive year. Meanwhile, Amazon climbed into the top five, reflecting the growing importance of e-commerce, while traditional giants like AT&T and ExxonMobil saw significant drops in rankings. This year's Global 2000 ranking illustrates the resilience and shifts within the U.S. corporate landscape amidst economic volatility.

title: Gunmaker Troy moving to Clarksville with 75 jobs, leaving Massachusetts over ‘changing climate’
summary: Firearms manufacturer Troy Industries is relocating its headquarters and manufacturing operations from West Springfield, Massachusetts, to Clarksville, Tennessee. This move, which represents a $7.2 million investment and 75 new jobs, is largely due to the "changing climate" for gunmakers in Massachusetts. The company is actively recruiting, focusing on veterans, women, and minorities, and anticipates contributing significantly to Clarksville's economic growth.

title: NHL, Amazon Web Services to debut advanced stats during playoffs
summary: The NHL and Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced the debut of two new advanced analytics, "shot analytics" and "save analytics," during the 2021 Stanley Cup Playoffs. These stats will be displayed as on-screen graphics and data visualizations, providing fans with deeper insights into player and team performance. Leveraging historical NHL data and real-time game activity, these analytics aim to enhance the broadcast viewing experience and offer new perspectives for fans, players, coaches, and broadcasters.

title: 2021 Ford F-150 and Mustang Mach-E Owners: New Features Coming Your Way
summary: Ford is rolling out a series of Power-Up software updates for its 2021 F-150 and Mustang Mach-E vehicles equipped with Sync 4. These over-the-air updates include bug fixes for issues like zone lighting and Android Auto connectivity, as well as enhancements to features like Apple CarPlay display and the native navigation system. New functionalities, such as the BlueCruise hands-free driving software and a drawing/gaming feature called Sketch or Notes for the Mach-E, are also being introduced, along with enhanced Amazon Alexa integration.

title: Alexa® Functionality Now Available for FirstEnergy Utility Customers
summary: FirstEnergy utility customers can now use Amazon's Alexa-enabled devices to access information about their electric bills. This new functionality provides details such as billing notifications, due dates, payment confirmations, and monthly/yearly billing comparisons at no additional cost. The company plans to add more features like kilowatt-hour usage comparisons and bill payment capabilities in the future.

title: XPO Logistics Increases Hiring Activity in North America to Meet Growing Logistics Demand
summary: XPO Logistics is recruiting for over 4,000 jobs across North America to meet the growing demand in its logistics business, driven by automation, outsourcing, and e-commerce. This hiring initiative precedes the planned spin-off of its logistics segment into GXO Logistics, Inc. The company is seeking material handlers, inventory specialists, and robotic maintenance technicians, offering competitive pay and benefits.

title: Transformers Kingdom Dinobot Concept Art by Ken Christiansen
summary: Ken Christiansen has revealed new concept art for the Transformers Kingdom Dinobot figure. The art includes detailed drawings of the Dinobot in its robot mode, commissioned in partnership with Hasbro, Inc. These designs are now available for viewing on Hasbro Pulse.

title: Polaris Warranty Program Faced Significant Challenges, 13 May 2021
summary: In 2012, Polaris faced a 34% premium rate increase on its Polaris Protection Plan due to an actuarial review by its third-party administrator. After, Inc. conducted an independent analysis, identifying significant errors in the carrier's methodology, particularly in how premiums were earned versus claims incurred. By presenting these findings, After, Inc. helped Polaris avoid the rate increase and subsequently moved Polaris to a fully in-house warranty company, saving millions and ensuring program stability.

title: Is TiVo done with streaming dongles? Not so fast
summary: Despite recent reports suggesting TiVo might be abandoning its streaming dongle business, a company spokesperson states that TiVo will continue to produce new Android TV dongles and improve the existing Stream 4K. The move comes as TiVo's parent company, Xperi, also explores embedding its software directly into smart TVs. The article highlights the potential of TiVo's streaming solution for cord-cutters and the competitive landscape of both streaming devices and smart TV platforms.

title: Polen Focus Growth Fund Purchased Amazon.com (AMZN), Should You Do the Same?
summary: Polen Capital's "Polen Focus Growth" fund purchased Amazon.com (AMZN) in February 2021, making it 5% of their portfolio, based on increased visibility into the company's free cash flow margins and future earnings growth from AWS and Advertising. The fund, which returned 1.81% in Q1 2021, highlighted Amazon's evolving profit drivers from e-commerce to higher-margin services. Despite past concerns about Amazon's fit with their guardrails, Polen Capital now believes these high-margin segments could drive over 30% annual earnings growth for the next five years.

title: Amdocs Acquires Sourced to Further Boost Communications Industry’s Move to the Cloud
summary: Amdocs has acquired Sourced Group, a leading global technology consultancy, to enhance its capabilities in helping the communications industry transition to the cloud. This acquisition expands Amdocs’ portfolio of cloud-native products and services, leveraging Sourced’s decade of experience in large-scale cloud transformations for high-end enterprises. The deal, valued at approximately $75 million in cash, is expected to be neutral to Amdocs' non-GAAP diluted earnings per share for fiscal year 2021.

title: Elasticsearch on AWS: Deploying Your First Managed Cluster
summary: This article explains how to deploy a managed Elasticsearch cluster on Amazon Web Services (AWS) using Amazon's managed Elasticsearch Service (Amazon ES). It covers the key features of Amazon ES, a step-by-step guide to creating a new domain, and methods for ingesting and searching data. Additionally, it addresses how Amazon ES manages various administrative tasks and its compatibility with open-source Elasticsearch APIs.

title: The Business Ethics Leadership Alliance Welcomes New Members, Amazon, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, and More While Recognizing Companies and Leaders With Exceptional Impact
summary: The Business Ethics Leadership Alliance (BELA) announced new member companies, including Amazon and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, significantly expanding its community to over 325 organizations. Ethisphere, BELA's founder, also recognized seven companies and individual leaders with BELA Impact Awards for their exceptional commitment to community engagement, growth, and transformation in ethical business practices. The awards highlight crucial contributions to the compliance and ethics profession amidst ongoing global challenges.

title: An FAQ on the Matter protocol
summary: This article provides an FAQ on the Matter protocol, which is a new smart home interoperability standard launched by major tech companies. It explains what Matter and Thread are, how they will affect existing smart home technologies like Zigbee and Z-Wave, and what the implications are for consumers, hardware manufacturers, and professional installers. The article also touches on the potential impact on open-source platforms like Home Assistant.

title: AT&T signing $43B deal to combine media business with Discovery
summary: AT&T announced a $43 billion deal to spin off its WarnerMedia content unit and merge it with Discovery, creating a new media giant. This move aims to better compete with streaming services like Netflix and Disney, with current AT&T shareholders retaining 71 percent of the new company. Discovery CEO David Zaslav will lead the combined entity, marking a significant strategic shift for AT&T.

title: HPE bets on Europe’s Gaia-X cloud and data services initiative
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is launching its HPE Solution Framework for Gaia-X, aligning with Europe's initiative to create a unified, data-privacy-protected cloud and data services ecosystem. Gaia-X aims to reduce Europe's reliance on non-European cloud providers by fostering an interoperable data exchange governed by European laws. HPE's framework, built on the HPE Ezmeral Software Platform, will help companies participate in this decentralized environment, emphasizing secure data operations and allowing businesses to maintain ownership and control over their data.

title: Wholesalers are testing out digital marketplaces
summary: The wholesale sector is increasingly adopting digital marketplace models, with large players like United Natural Foods Inc. launching their own platforms to attract hyperlocal vendors and serve small-to-medium businesses. This shift is driven by the pandemic's impact on traditional trade shows and the development of sophisticated software that can handle the complexities of B2B transactions. The trend suggests a significant movement towards online B2B marketplaces, mirroring the growth seen in consumer-oriented e-commerce.

title: Walmart sales boosted by US stimulus cheques
summary: Walmart reported better-than-expected first-quarter results, driven by US government stimulus payments that encouraged shoppers to spend on clothing and home goods. The company raised its annual earnings forecast and observed a 6 percent increase in comparable sales and a 37 percent rise in online sales. CEO Doug McMillon noted a strong desire among customers to return to shopping, contributing to increased transactions and sales in categories like travel items.

title: Woodside Energy adds actual robots into code pipeline stages
summary: Woodside Energy has detailed its continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipeline for robot code, which involves rigorous testing in labs and staging areas before deployment to remote production sites like its Pluto LNG facility. This methodical approach ensures the robots perform as expected in the field, with the long-term goal of enabling remote operations without human supervision. The company aims for these robots to eventually interact with their environment beyond just monitoring.

title: Where and how to buy Alphabet (GOOGL) stock
summary: This guide provides a comprehensive overview for newcomers interested in buying Alphabet (GOOGL) stock. It covers essential steps such as choosing a trading platform, funding an account, deciding investment amounts, and differentiating between buying shares or ETFs. The article also explains various order types and the importance of monitoring GOOGL's performance.

title: JBG SMITH Secures Approval for National Landing Apartments
summary: JBG SMITH has received final approvals for two residential projects at 2000 and 2001 S. Bell St. in Arlington, Va.'s National Landing area. These projects will comprise 758 units and 22,000 square feet of retail space across two towers, with construction potentially starting in early 2022. The development is part of a community benefits agreement with Arlington County, including dedicating affordable housing units and contributing to an affordable housing fund.

title: Amazon sets opening date for its first grocery store in D.C. area. More locations poised to follow.
summary: Amazon has announced the opening date for its first grocery store in the D.C. area, located in Franconia, Virginia, at the Festival at Manchester Lakes shopping center. The store is scheduled to open on May 24 and marks the e-commerce giant's first physical grocery presence in the region, with more locations expected to follow. This development was initially reported last August under the codename "Mendel’s Market."

title: Target Sales Hit $23.8B in Q1
summary: Target reported a significant increase in its Q1 2021 sales, reaching $23.8 billion, a 23% rise from the previous year. This growth was largely attributed to an enthusiastic return to in-store shopping by consumers, with same-store sales up 18%. The company's "stores-as-hubs" model continued to be effective, fulfilling three-quarters of digital orders and over 95% of same-day services.

title: Amazon.com faces five new racial, gender bias lawsuits
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is facing five new lawsuits filed by women in corporate and warehouse management roles, alleging gender bias, racial bias, or both. The lawsuits accuse Amazon of favoring men, allowing workplace denigration, and retaliating against complainants. Amazon denies the accusations and states it does not tolerate discrimination.

title: JPMorgan launching business arm to address cost, quality of employer healthcare
summary: JPMorgan Chase is launching a new business arm called Morgan Health to address the cost and quality of employer-sponsored healthcare, building on lessons learned from its dissolved Haven venture with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway. JPMorgan plans to invest $250 million in healthcare solutions, initially focusing on its own employees before aiming to serve as a model for other employers. Morgan Health will partner with healthcare organizations, including CVS Health, to enhance care options and boost health equity.

title: JPMorgan Chase launches new health-care business after winding down Amazon-Berkshire venture
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced the launch of Morgan Health, a new health-care business aimed at improving medical care quality for its 165,000 U.S. employees and their families. This initiative comes after the disbandment of Haven, a joint venture with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway. Morgan Health will be led by Dan Mendelson and will have $250 million for venture investments in promising health-care solutions, focusing on direct partnerships with providers and preventative care.

title: JPMorgan Chase Launches In-House Healthcare Company, Morgan Health
summary: JPMorgan Chase has launched its own healthcare company, Morgan Health, after the dissolution of its joint venture with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway. The new unit will focus on improving medical care for the banking giant's 165,000 employees and their families, with an initial investment of $250 million earmarked for promising healthcare solutions. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon stated the goal is to address long-standing healthcare issues and achieve significant improvements.

title: Sprouts accelerates efforts to stand out with unique products
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market is intensifying its focus on selling unique, wellness-oriented products not found at other retailers, aiming to differentiate itself and attract "health enthusiasts." CEO Jack Sinclair stated that the company is positioning itself as a specialty food business rather than a conventional grocer, which allows it to thrive in its e-commerce operations with higher-margin, attribute-based products. This strategy has led to a significant portion of its inventory being unique compared to competitors, and Sprouts sees opportunities as other retailers like Whole Foods diversify into more conventional offerings.

title: Oracle, office deal flow, remote work all key topics of Williamson Inc. economic development panel
summary: A panel of economic developers organized by Williamson Inc. discussed key trends affecting the area, including rising office deal flow, the competition between Oracle and Amazon, and the impact of remote work. A key takeaway was the challenge and opportunity for states to support companies with remote workers. The discussion also touched upon recent job relocations and local business surveys.

title: Schlumberger Announces Collaboration with AWS to Deploy DELFI Petrotechnical Suite on AWS
summary: Schlumberger announced a collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to deploy its DELFI* cognitive E&P environment and core petrotechnical applications on the cloud. This partnership will give AWS customers access to Schlumberger's AI-enhanced applications and AWS's high-performance computing infrastructure, enabling faster and better decision-making from subsurface data. The goal is to expand access to the DELFI environment, allowing more customers to leverage advanced digital solutions for improved productivity and performance in the energy sector.

title: JD Logistics IPO plans fail to lift JD.com shares
summary: Despite its logistics arm, JD Logistics, preparing for a substantial IPO that could raise up to $3.4 billion, JD.com's share price has been on a downward trend since February. The company's stock has underperformed the S&P 500 over the past 12 months and has seen further decline since the IPO's approval. The JD Logistics IPO is viewed as a critical test for investor interest in Chinese tech stocks, a sector that has faced regulatory scrutiny and declining performance in recent months.

title: Amazon shutting down Prime Now, moving two-hour delivery to Amazon app
summary: Amazon is discontinuing its standalone Prime Now app, integrating its two-hour delivery services for essential goods and groceries directly into the main Amazon app and website. This move aims to streamline the shopping experience for customers by offering all of Amazon's services from a single platform. The integration will allow users to shop from Whole Foods and other local stores with expedited delivery.

title: JPMorgan Chase unveils solo healthcare venture
summary: JPMorgan Chase has launched Morgan Health, a new healthcare venture with $250 million to invest in innovations aimed at improving medical care quality, health equity, and cost control for its 165,000 employees and their families. This initiative comes four months after the dissolution of Haven, a joint healthcare venture involving Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan. Led by Dan Mendelson, Morgan Health will focus on digital tools, analytics, preventative care for conditions like maternal health, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes, and will collaborate with other organizations rather than building new technologies from scratch.

title: P&G Earns Seventh Straight Gartner Supply Chain Mastery Award
summary: P&G has received its seventh consecutive Gartner Supply Chain Mastery Award, an achievement that highlights its long-term excellence in supply chain management. This recognition comes despite the extreme disruptions caused by the pandemic, which tested P&G's supply chain significantly. P&G is one of only five companies, including Apple, Amazon, McDonald’s, and Unilever, to be recognized in the elite "Master" category, which acknowledges consistent top performance over many years.

title: The Curious Case of a Toys ‘R’ Us Killer
summary: This article traces the unexpected connection between Vornado Realty, a prominent real estate firm, and the demise of Toys 'R' Us, highlighting Vornado's own twisting corporate history. It reveals how Vornado, originally an appliance manufacturer and then a discount retailer (Two Guys), transformed into a real estate giant by leveraging its suburban land holdings. The piece argues that Vornado's trajectory and engagement with Toys 'R' Us exemplify broader, long-term trends of offshoring and financialization within the American economy.

title: Amazon nears deal to buy MGM Studios
summary: Amazon is reportedly close to acquiring MGM Holdings for nearly $9 billion, marking its second-largest acquisition. The deal would significantly bolster Amazon's streaming service, Prime Video, with MGM's extensive library of classic films and TV shows including the James Bond franchise. This move reflects the increasing consolidation in the media industry driven by the streaming wars.

title: Huge Fort Worth shipping hub changes hands
summary: A large Fort Worth industrial shipping hub, leased to Amazon, has been sold to a real estate investment trust. The Interstate Crossing distribution center, over 1 million square feet, was developed by Hunt Southwest and acquired by a fund organized by San Diego-based Realty Income Corp. This sale reflects the ongoing strong investor interest in warehouse and distribution properties, especially significant in one of the country's largest warehouse building markets.

title: Amazon deal to acquire MGM movie studio could come Tuesday
summary: Amazon is reportedly close to finalizing a deal to acquire Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) movie studio as early as Tuesday for nearly $9 billion. This acquisition would significantly bolster Amazon's Prime Video streaming service by adding MGM's extensive library, which includes popular franchises like James Bond, Pink Panther, RoboCop, and Rocky, as well as films like "The Silence of the Lambs." The move represents Amazon's largest push into Hollywood and its biggest acquisition since Whole Foods in 2017.

title: Twilio CEO Jeff Lawson reveals how founding StubHub and a skate shop led him to Twilio
summary: Twilio CEO Jeff Lawson shares his entrepreneurial journey, beginning with a childhood fascination with computers and early ventures like the app Notes4Free and co-founding StubHub. He discusses how his diverse experiences, including even opening a skate shop, eventually led him to found Twilio, driven by a passion for software's ability to iterate and serve customers. Lawson emphasizes key lessons learned such as ruthlessly removing friction for customer attraction, the importance of listening to customers even regarding sales teams, and the responsibility of giving back to society.

title: Oracle debuts its first Arm-based cloud instances
summary: Oracle has launched its first Arm-based cloud instances, OCI Ampere A1 Compute, offering customers more flexibility and high performance at lower costs for general-purpose and cloud-native workloads. This move signifies Oracle's increased investment in the Arm ecosystem, providing a compelling alternative to x86-based instances and competing with rival cloud providers by offering attractive pricing and scaling options. The company is also expanding developer resources and tools to encourage Arm-based application development on its cloud platform, including free tier offerings and a new development stack.

title: Oracle launches Arm-based cloud computing service using Ampere chips
summary: Oracle Corp has launched a new cloud computing service that utilizes Arm-based data center chips from Ampere Computing, becoming the second major cloud provider after Amazon Web Services to offer such a service. This move aims to provide customers with more value and choice, challenging the long-standing dominance of Intel and AMD in the cloud chip market. Oracle is also promoting initiatives to expand software compatibility with Arm chips.

title: Microsoft teams up with Accenture and Goldman Sachs to create energy efficient software
summary: Microsoft, Accenture, and Goldman Sachs, along with other organizations, are forming the Green Software Foundation to develop and share methods for creating software that produces fewer carbon emissions in data centers. Data centers currently account for about 1% of global electricity demand, projected to rise significantly, prompting the need for "green software engineering" skills. The foundation aims to build tools, establish standards for measuring software's climate impact, and provide training for engineers.

title: App Store Arguments
summary: This article analyzes the legal, pragmatic, duopoly, moral, and anti-steering arguments surrounding Apple's App Store, particularly in light of the Epic Games v. Apple trial. The author suggests that while Apple has a strong legal standing based on Supreme Court precedents, there are valid counterarguments regarding competition, developer relationships, and the overall health of the iOS ecosystem. The piece concludes by suggesting Apple should consider conceding some ground to developers to foster a more open and innovative environment, especially given global regulatory scrutiny.

title: JPMorgan Chase Launches New Unit to Improve Care Quality for Employees
summary: JPMorgan Chase is investing up to $250 million in a new venture called Morgan Health, aiming to improve health outcomes and promote health equity for its employees. This initiative follows the dissolution of its previous Haven collaborative with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway. Morgan Health plans to collaborate with leading healthcare organizations to develop new models for care improvement, focusing on behavioral health, disease management, and addressing healthcare disparities.

title: Globe, PLDT say content now important part of business
summary: Globe Telecom and PLDT view content creation and bundling as a critical component for future growth and customer retention. Globe expects its content business and "customer-first" initiatives to drive growth, expanding on existing partnerships and producing original content through Globe Studios. PLDT's Chairman, Manuel V. Pangilinan, emphasizes the need for synergy among media companies within the group to provide converged content, particularly video, and enhance the overall customer experience for wireless users.

title: Amazon agrees to buy MGM film studio for $8.45 billion
authors: ['By Asa Hiken; By Adrianne Pasquarelli; By E.J. Schultz; By Brian Bonilla; By Parker Herren']
summary: Amazon has reached an agreement to acquire MGM film studio for $8.45 billion. This acquisition will significantly expand Amazon's content library, bolstering its presence in the entertainment industry and providing a vast catalog for its Prime Video service. The deal highlights the increasing consolidation in the media landscape.

title: Amazon buys MGM as D.C. suit charges its monopolistic practices violate antitrust laws
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of MGM for $8.5 billion, capitalizing on the film industry's struggles. This comes as Washington D.C. Attorney General Karl Racine filed an antitrust suit against Amazon, alleging that its contractual terms force third-party sellers to offer products at lower prices on Amazon, thereby harming both sellers and customers through inflated fees and prices. The lawsuit highlights Amazon's significant control over online retail and questions the monopolistic practices of platform companies.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Carl Icahn, Warren Buffett, Bill Ackman, Ray Dalio, Elliott Management, Assurant Inc. (AIZ), Innoviva Inc (INVA), and More
summary: This article covers recent news in the hedge fund and insider trading world, featuring prominent investors like Carl Icahn, Bill Ackman, and Elliott Management. Key topics include Carl Icahn's activism, Bill Ackman's SPAC deal and market outlook, Elliott Management's strategy regarding GlaxoSmithKline, and Amazon's acquisition of MGM bolstering hedge fund profits. The article also touches on increasing data demands driving hedge fund operational costs and hedge fund assets reaching a new high of over $4 trillion.

title: Amazon's major acquisitions over the years
summary: Amazon has acquired MGM for $8.45 billion, marking its second-largest acquisition and deepening its push into entertainment. This deal grants Amazon a vast library of films and TV shows for its Prime video streaming service. The article outlines Amazon's significant acquisitions over the past two decades, including Whole Foods Market, Twitch, Ring, and PillPack.

title: Amazon shareholder meeting: Push to put an hourly worker on board
summary: Labour activists are pushing for an hourly worker to join Amazon's board of directors at its shareholder meeting, following a failed union drive. The proposal, backed by Oxfam America and recommended by proxy adviser ISS, aims to elevate employee concerns amidst allegations of monopolistic practices and environmental racism. However, Amazon's board opposes the resolution, and some proxy advisers are concerned about board independence.

title: Apple Faces Criticism Over Its Cooperation With China
summary: Apple is facing increasing criticism for its cooperation with Chinese laws, which involve sharing consumer data and censoring content, amid a wider technological and economic competition between the U.S. and China. The article also discusses the US Senate's "Endless Frontier Act" aimed at countering China's tech advancements, China's efforts to influence Latin American and African telecom markets, and its crackdown on cryptocurrency and its own tech giants.

title: MGM to Be Acquired by Amazon for $8.45 Billion
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of Beverly Hills-based Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Studios Inc. for $8.45 billion. This deal gives Amazon access to MGM's extensive library of 4,000 films and 17,000 television shows, aiming to enhance Prime Video's competitive edge against other streaming services. The acquisition, subject to regulatory approval, will allow Amazon to "reimagine and develop" MGM's intellectual property for the 21st century.

title: American Express Sets Up Autonomous Checkout At Barclays Center
summary: American Express has launched an autonomous checkout store at Brooklyn's Barclays Center, home of the New York Nets, to allow cardholders to quickly purchase concessions and merchandise. This initiative, similar to Amazon Go stores, aims to enhance customer experience by reducing wait times and addressing contactless payment preferences heightened by COVID-19. The store tracks items using weight-sensitive shelf sensors, with entry exclusive to Amex cardholders.

title: FOS PM: Dick's Crushes Earnings
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods reported record first-quarter earnings, with revenue soaring 119% to $2.92 billion and net income reaching $361.8 million. This surge was attributed to increased interest in golf and a resurgence in team sports, alongside strong performance in outdoor activities and athleisure. Additionally, Amazon acquired MGM Studios for $8.45 billion to expand its media library, and billionaire Joseph Tsai added a Las Vegas lacrosse expansion team to his sports portfolio.

title: During Investor Day, Kontoor Details the Benefits of Casting a Wide Net
summary: Kontoor Brands held its first-ever virtual investor day, outlining strategies for significant revenue and consumer growth for its Lee and Wrangler brands. Despite initial COVID-19 impacts, both brands are bouncing back, with plans for geographic expansion, category extensions, and digital initiatives. The company anticipates substantial e-commerce revenue increases and aims to boost Wrangler's revenue to $1.7 billion and Lee's to $1 billion by 2023 through product elevation, new categories like outdoor wear, and strategic collaborations.

title: Amazon brings James Bond, Rocky to fight Netflix with $8.5 bln MGM buy
summary: Amazon is acquiring MGM, the studio behind James Bond and Rocky, for $8.45 billion to expand its content library and compete more effectively with streaming rivals like Netflix and Disney+. This acquisition will bolster Amazon's Prime Video service by adding a vast catalog of films and TV shows, including valuable intellectual property that Amazon plans to reimagine for the 21st century. The deal, Amazon's second-largest after Whole Foods, highlights the ongoing consolidation in the media industry as companies vie for compelling content to attract and retain streaming subscribers.

title: Sony Pictures Not for Sale, Says CEO Yoshida Kenichiro
summary: Sony Group CEO Yoshida Kenichiro has stated that Sony Pictures is not for sale and will not be spun off, despite industry speculation fueled by recent mergers and acquisitions like Amazon's purchase of MGM. Sony's strategy involves operating as an independent studio, supplying content to streamers, and leveraging its various entertainment divisions, such as gaming and anime, to create content. The company has secured licensing deals with Netflix and Disney+ and plans to produce more films for direct release on streaming platforms while retaining ownership.

title: Bitcoin and Ethereum are now, decentralized apps are the future
summary: Olaf Carlson-Wee, founder of Polychain Capital, believes decentralized web applications (DAOs) will be the next major trend in crypto, following the success of Bitcoin, Ethereum, and DeFi. He envisions decentralized versions of popular social media and chat apps owned by communities via crypto tokens, starting with simpler applications like photo hosting or messaging apps before moving to more complex platforms. Carlson-Wee also notes the rapid growth of decentralized exchanges (DEXes) like Uniswap, highlighting their collision course with regulators due to potential money laundering concerns.

title: S&P 500 trading guide: constituents, market hours and h
summary: This guide provides an in-depth look at the S&P 500, a key benchmark for U.S. stock market performance. It covers the index's constituents, listing criteria, calculation methods, factors affecting its price, and average annual returns. The article also details various ways to trade the S&P 500, including CFDs, futures, options, and ETFs, and discusses strategies for shorting the index.

title: In Current M&A Moment, Lionsgate A Prime Target As CEO Jon Feltheimer Downplays “Concept Of Scale”
summary: Lionsgate CEO Jon Feltheimer acknowledged the recent media merger deals as a validation of content value but emphasized the company's focus on its own strategy, downplaying the "concept of scale." Despite this, Lionsgate is widely considered a prime takeover target due to its valuable library, Starz subscribers, and manageable size, especially following major deals like Amazon's acquisition of MGM. Analysts suggest it could be worth at least $8 billion.

title: How Vimeo went from CollegeHumor side project to a multibillion-dollar company
summary: Vimeo, once a side project of CollegeHumor, has grown into a multibillion-dollar public software company. Initially acquired by IAC almost by accident, Vimeo pivoted from being a YouTube competitor to building video software for businesses under the leadership of Anjali Sud. The company recently went public with over 200 million users and 1.6 million paying subscribers, generating substantial revenue.

title: Hundreds of Companies Unite to Oppose Voting Limits, but Others Abstain (Published 2021)
summary: Hundreds of major companies, including Amazon, Google, G.M., and Starbucks, signed a statement opposing "any discriminatory legislation" that makes it harder to vote. This initiative, organized by former American Express CEO Kenneth Chenault and Merck CEO Kenneth Frazier, marks the largest show of corporate solidarity against Republican-led efforts to enact new election rules nationwide. The move comes despite calls from senior Republicans for companies to avoid political issues.

title: Higg launches customer-facing transparency program
summary: The Sustainable Apparel Coalition (SAC) and its partner Higg have launched the first phase of a transparency program to share data on the environmental impact of apparel and footwear products, starting with materials. The program introduces the Higg Index Sustainability Profile and Materials seal, utilizing independently reviewed data from the Higg Materials Sustainability Index (MSI). Brands like Norrøna and Salomon are early adopters, with plans to expand the initiative to include manufacturing, corporate responsibility, and social data by early 2023.

title: Docker Honeypot Reveals Cryptojacking as Most Common Cloud Threat
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 deployed a honeypot mimicking a misconfigured Docker daemon to observe cloud-related threats between March and April 2021. The research found that over 75% of the 850 attacks recorded were cryptojacking, with Kinsing being the most prevalent malware. Attackers exploit misconfigured Docker daemons to gain full control, deploy malicious containers, and often escalate privileges to the host system.

title: Amazon Fresh opens first D.C.-area location. In this full-size grocery store, no cashier is needed.
summary: Amazon has opened its first Amazon Fresh grocery store in the D.C. area, located at the Manchester Lakes shopping center in Franconia. The store offers a cashier-less shopping experience, where Prime customers can use Amazon Dash carts. Shoppers can also use Alexa for in-store assistance.

title: AR’s role in shopping poised to swell in next 5 years, Publicis and Snap find
summary: A new study by Publicis Media, Snap, and Alter Agents indicates that augmented reality (AR) significantly influences consumer shopping habits, especially among Snapchat users who are 56% more likely to use branded AR lenses and increase their likelihood to purchase. The pandemic accelerated AR adoption in shopping, and three out of four respondents believe AR will play a larger role in retail over the next five years. Snap continues to expand its commerce capabilities, integrating AR into new features and partnerships to meet evolving consumer expectations and leverage AR's increasing utility in the shopping journey.

title: Coinbase crypto partner Circle raises $440 million from Fidelity and others
summary: Cryptocurrency startup Circle, a Coinbase partner, has successfully raised $440 million in new funding from investors including Fidelity and FTX. This funding round highlights the growing investor appetite for crypto companies, coinciding with Coinbase's market debut and Circle's own plans to go public via a SPAC at a $4 billion valuation. Circle is increasingly focusing on its USD Coin (USDC) stablecoin, which has seen significant growth and adoption for digital payments.

title: Mountain View self-driving trucking company Aurora Innovation expanding in Dallas area
summary: Aurora Innovation, a self-driving trucking company backed by Amazon and Hyundai, is expanding its operations in the Dallas area to accommodate its growing workforce. This expansion comes less than a year after the company announced its intention to test its self-driving technology in Texas. Aurora Innovation's CEO, Chris Urmson, previously led Google's self-driving car unit.

title: How Nvidia plans to own the data center with AI
summary: Nvidia aims to revolutionize enterprise computing by making data centers run 10 times faster at one-tenth the cost, leveraging its strong position in AI architectures. The company plans to disrupt Intel's x86 dominance through Arm-based architectures, integrated chip designs, and a compelling software consumption model. The article highlights Nvidia's strategic moves, financial standing, and the potential impact of its proposed acquisition of Arm Ltd. on the data center market.

title: Everything to know about the Huntington Shopping Center renovation plans
summary: The Huntington Shopping Center is set for a $40 million renovation, which will see much of the existing structure demolished to make way for a new building anchored by a Whole Foods grocery store. The plans include significant landscaping updates, new facades, wider sidewalks, and two potential standalone buildings for restaurants or high-end retail, despite an overall 22% reduction in retail space. While the architectural renderings have been approved, the site plan is still awaiting final approval, and the future of existing tenants remains uncertain, though Nordstrom Rack is confirmed to close.

title: Fifth Third Bank warns of text scams about online banking
summary: Fifth Third Bank is warning customers about text message scams claiming a "temporary hold" has been placed on their online banking accounts. These texts are fraudulent, and the bank advises caution against clicking links or sharing personal information. Customers should be suspicious of urgent requests for account numbers or Social Security numbers and can call Fifth Third directly if unsure about a message's legitimacy.

title: Grab, GoTo, and Sea: Who Has the Formula For Superapp Supremacy in Southeast Asia?
summary: This article analyzes the three-way battle for superapp supremacy in Southeast Asia between Grab, GoTo, and Sea Limited. It profiles each company, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses, and scores them across five strategic areas: ridesharing and food delivery, entertainment, ecommerce, payment apps, and founder/CEO leadership. The author concludes that while the race appears even, each company has distinct advantages, with Grab strong in payments and regional expansion, Sea in entertainment and e-commerce, and GoTo's strength lying in Indonesia.
